text:
ana (SRE): heads up — prod prometheus remote_write errors spiked at 07:10 UTC after the GPU node-exporter rollout. lots of 400s from cortex-eu and series count jumped ~15x.

ben (infra): link to grafana? what query are you running?

ana (SRE): grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/ABCD1234/remote-write-overview
query i used: `sum by(cluster) (prometheus_tsdb_head_series)`
output: head_series for gpu-prod went from ~80k -> ~1.2M over ~5m. remote_write logs:
```
level=error ts=2026-03-18T07:11:02Z caller=client.go:345 err="remote_write: failed to post: 400 Bad Request: max_series limit exceeded: 1200000"
```

lin (platform): do we know which metric exploded? driver or exporter?

ana (SRE): looks like node-exporter v1.12.0 added per-accelerator metrics: labels `accel_id` and `accel_core`. lots of new series like `gpu_power{accel_id="0"}`, `gpu_power{accel_id="1"}`, etc across pods. per-pod cardinality multiplied by num-accels.

monitoring-bot: ALERT firing: PrometheusRemoteWriteErrors (severity=P1) — remote_write error rate > 5/min for cortex-eu cluster

ryan (oncall): are we also seeing network timeouts? could be retries amplifying load to remote_write. check tcpstats to cortex-eu.

ana (SRE): running tcpdump on prometheus-sidecar egress, seeing retransmits and higher RTT to cortex-eu endpoint after the spike: 
```
14:11:05.123456 IP prometheus-01 > cortex-eu: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12467, ack 9876, win 64240, length 122
14:11:05.223456 IP prometheus-01 > cortex-eu: Flags [P.], seq ... (retransmission)
```
RTT baseline 30ms -> 240ms for several minutes. might be regional networking flapping + amplified payloads.

ben (infra): two quick mitigations: 1) drop high-cardinality labels at scrape (metric_relabel_configs) OR 2) rollback exporter on GPU nodes. which is faster?

lin (platform): for labels on metrics we must use `metric_relabel_configs` (not `relabel_configs`). example to drop accel labels by metric name pattern: 
```
metric_relabel_configs:
- source_labels: [__name__]
  regex: "gpu_.*"
  action: keep
- source_labels: [accel_id]
  action: drop
```
but that will drop accel_id for all metrics — maybe better to drop the whole per-accel metrics set: 
```
metric_relabel_configs:
- regex: 'gpu_core_temp|gpu_power|gpu_utilization'
  action: drop
```
(put the exact names in regex)

ana (SRE): rolling back exporter would be surgical but takes kube rollout time and patching a daemonset. i'm patching metric_relabel_configs on the gpu scrape job now to drop `accel_id` and the obvious per-accel metric names. applying to scrape config in next 30s.

ben (infra): thanks — also throttle remote_write concurrency as a safety net: set `max_concurrent_requests: 4` and bump `queue_config.max_samples_per_send` lower to reduce burst size.

lin (platform): noted — will open a followup to add exporter version gating to our daemonset job so major metric surface changes require a canary.

monitoring-bot: UPD: PrometheusRemoteWriteErrors alert rate decreasing.

ana (SRE): metric_relabel_configs applied at 07:14:20 UTC. watching head_series and http 400s.

ryan (oncall): nice. can someone open a quick PR to infra-config with the relabel snippet and rollback notes? i want an audit trail and a postmortem section.

ana (SRE): on it — will include timelines, exporter version, and recommended permanent fix (drop per-accel metrics or normalise accel label).

monitoring-bot: ALERT resolved: PrometheusRemoteWriteErrors (was firing for 18m)

ben (infra): followup actions: 1) rollback exporter in canary until we have a proper relabel plan, 2) add metric relabel to gpu scrape permanently, 3) add SLO guard for head_series increase to avoid silent runaway.

lin (platform): I'll draft the PR for gating and add automated test to detect >3x series jump on deployment.

ryan (oncall): thanks team — log this as incident-2026-03-18-gpu-exporter-cardinality in postmortems. :+1:

ana (SRE): done — incident note created and PR opened: https://git.internal/infra/2245

ben (infra): moving to monitoring follow-up checklist.

monitoring-bot: thread closed by monitoring-bot
